reason: A is a clear tall-format adaptation: the bottle is large and prominent, the headline is big and wraps into two lines with a small 'fizz' orphan. The subcopy is readable, the CTA is large and close to its copy, and the circles are kept as decor. It has minor flaws: the bottom third is empty, the CTA sits tight under the subcopy, and the green circle runs behind the logo. B shrinks everything: the bottle is tiny and the headline is small and weak. The subcopy and CTA label are tiny, and the large gaps between elements mean related items don't group. The green circle overlaps the SOLSTICE wordmark and the peach circle crowds the CTA. It looks like a shrunk copy with a lot of dead space.

A: the CTA 'Find a Store' is tiny (about 95x22 px) and jammed under the headline, so the CTA is buried. There's a big dead gap between the bag and the headline, and the CTA sits close to the bottom edge. The olive circle in the top-left is clipped and crowds the CITRINE logo. B: the CTA is a properly sized pill, clearly tappable and well grouped with the headline. The bag is sized well and the spacing is more even. Flaws: the bag overlaps the green circle slightly awkwardly, the olive circle at the bottom-left is cut off and arbitrary, and the 'fizz' wrap leaves an orphan-ish line.

A keeps the full-bleed dark header band and the original order, and its headline is well wrapped and centred. Flaws: the divider is moved below the body copy, there are big dead gaps around the headline and above the body, and the logo and fine print are tiny. B's header band is inset and does not reach the right edge, which breaks the brand frame and looks like a bug. B also pushes 'Ships late June' far from the CTA, adds a wide gap between the eyebrow and the headline, and leaves the legal text with an orphaned last line. Its headline is slightly bigger, but B is the less polished of the two.

A: the logo is shrunk to a tiny speck stranded in a big dark block, so the brand is effectively lost. The divider is orphaned in empty space, and the headline crowds the canvas top and right edges. The bottom row (body, CTA, 'Ships late June') is scattered and misaligned, and the CTA label and legal text are tiny. B: the logo stays legible and the dark band, headline, body and CTA keep the original reading order. Flaws: the right half is a dead empty area, the divider is stranded there, and the dark band covers only the left half. The legal line is tiny and floats detached from the content, and the CTA is smallish.

A: headline crammed into 8 lines, the divider floats far above it, and body copy and the CTA are jammed at the bottom edge. The CTA is small and left-aligned with 'Ships late June' stranded beside it, and the logo bar is cramped. B: the logo bar stops short of the right edge (looks cropped and off-centre), and the body sits tight under the headline. It does keep a centered, readable stack with a prominent CTA, 'Ships late June' placed under the button, and more breathing room, so it is less broken.

A: the headline is pushed far from the product and the CTA is stranded at the far right edge. The tagline is tiny, and the two tag pills sit offset below, centered under nothing. The Free Delivery badge floats in the top corner. GROVE is centered over the headline instead of aligned with it. The layout is scattered with big dead gaps, though nothing collides. B: everything is crammed into a short stack. GROVE sits below the headline, so the order is wrong. The body text is tiny. The CTA button is small and weak, and the four pills are jammed together. The product circle is clipped at the left edge. The text is very tight, but it is a coherent, aligned left-to-right block with a clear headline, and the logo, headline and pills share one left edge.

A stacks the headline over the CTA, with the button at a readable size and the hierarchy intact. But the layout is very tight vertically: the headline sits almost against the top edge and the button nearly touches the bottom. B has a huge headline with almost no margin at the left and bottom. Its CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill with illegible label text, stranded at the far right edge and detached from the headline, so the CTA is buried.

A: the headline breaks as 'Bubbles,' alone on line one, then 'botanicals and a' and 'little sunshine.'. That gives an awkward, ragged wrap that splits the phrase and differs from the original's rhythm. It is large and well centred vertically, but the top margin (~35px) is tight. The button is small relative to the headline. B: it keeps the original's line breaks ('Bubbles, botanicals / and a little / sunshine.'), so it reads as the same design with a clean, balanced rag. It has comfortable margins. Flaws: the block sits slightly low (bottom margin ~25px against ~70px at top), the headline is a bit small for the wide banner, and the CTA text is tiny.

Both keep the same orange, serif headline and dark pill CTA, and both read cleanly. A is slightly better balanced, with about 130px above the headline and 65px below the button. Its gap between headline and CTA (~95px) is a bit loose, and the CTA is small next to the headline. B groups the headline and CTA more tightly, but it leaves ~175px of empty space on top and only ~50px under the button, so the block sits low and the CTA feels close to the bottom edge. Neither adds any new design intent.

A puts the SOLSTICE brand below the headline and the tagline overlaps the pink circle. The CTA is off-axis and crowds the tagline. The pills are tiny and illegible (about 5px text), their order is reversed, and the left half of the canvas is empty. B keeps a sensible reading order (brand, headline, tagline, CTA, pills) and the pills are legible, in the original order. Its flaws: the headline starts left of the other elements' edge and is cramped near the right edge, the tagline runs across the circle edge, the CTA floats right and isn't aligned with the left column, and the SOLSTICE wordmark is small and sits on the circle.

A keeps the original order (brand, headline, subline, pills) and its text is large and legible, with the headline dominant. Flaws: the CTA is offset on its own right-hand line and loosely related to the pills. The headline runs very close to the right edge. Circles sit behind SOLSTICE and the headline with little contrast cost. B reverses the hierarchy: SOLSTICE sits below the headline and above the subline. The pills are tiny and unreadable, and their order is reversed from the original (Honey Rosemary first). The CTA straddles the peach circle and is not aligned to the text column. The left side is a large empty area with only a circle in it.

A: left edges are ragged — the logo and headline sit at x≈88, the subhead at 70 and the pills at 65/106/345. The button is off-axis, the pills are staggered with no alignment, and the headline is wrapped into three lines over the circle edge. The bottom is empty and the legal line is indented. B: has a clean shared left margin, a tidy two-line headline, and the CTA beside the subhead. The pills sit in one row, but the order is reversed from the original. There are big dead gaps between headline and subhead and around the pills, the legal text is tiny, and the logo/headline sit awkwardly on the circle edge.

A has a clean left axis, a strong headline, readable text and chips in one row. Its flaws are a big dead gap between headline and subcopy, a CTA wedged beside the subcopy instead of below it, chips in reversed order, and tiny legal text. B has a cramped, ragged lower half: the CTA is centred while everything else is left-aligned, and the three chips are scattered at three different offsets and sizes with almost-touching edges. The legal text is off-axis and the headline overlaps the circle. B reads as jumbled and unintentional.

A: content is a small cluster floating mid-canvas with huge dead space below (about 35% empty) and a smaller empty band on top. Bottle is tiny and the secondary copy nearly touches the bottle's circle, so it reads as a shrunk copy. B: fills the tall format with a clear top-to-bottom order of eyebrow, headline, copy, CTA, then bottle, and the headline and CTA are strong. Flaws: the CTA sits tight to the body copy and the bottle, the bottle is left-of-centre and off the text axis, the circle is cropped at the edge, and the bottle's neck/shoulder shape looks slightly distorted.

A keeps a large readable serif headline, legible subcopy and a big CTA, but the logo circle is jammed into the top-left corner and cropped by the canvas edge. The subcopy is indented off the headline's left edge, NEW and Try It are right-aligned and ragged, and the bottom third is empty. B has a tiny headline and illegible subcopy. The product bottle is mis-rendered (outline-only, with the label bar floating), and the logo circle is orphaned as a cropped blob at the bottom-left. NEW and Try It are tiny and the CTA is weak, with large dead areas. Hierarchy has collapsed.

A: the headline is tiny and floats at the top, away from the huge circle. The bottle is stranded in the middle of the circle. The CTA is small, and 'Out now.' is detached and floats far from it. The result is weak hierarchy, a product that dominates the headline, and the headline sitting above the product with dead space around it. B: the headline is large and bold, and the CTA is big and clear, so the hierarchy is strong. Flaws: the product circle is cropped at the top-left corner and its bottle text is tiny, 'Out now.' is dark on orange with a low contrast, the left edges are misaligned (headline vs 'Out now.'), and the circle is cramped against the edge. It is still the stronger, more readable layout.

A: the RSVP button is tiny and indistinguishable from the tag pills, so the CTA is buried. The tags and CTA sit in one row with equal weight, the logo is tiny, the 'Solstice presents' kicker is minuscule and far from the title, and the layout is scattered with the mascot floating bottom-left. B: it keeps the original's centred hierarchy and the CTA is large and clear. But the tags are scattered, with 'Free entry' orphaned far from 'All ages' and 'Tastings'. The footer text is jammed against the placeholder asset. The date block is crowded in the bottom-left and the bottom area is cramped. Both are flawed; B is less bad because of its stronger CTA and headline hierarchy.

A: The quote is large and clearly the dominant element, and the logo stays anchored bottom-left as in the original. The flaws are the attribution indented about 22px from the quote text's left edge, a quote mark that matches neither edge, and an attribution that nearly touches the circle. The bottle sits left of centre in a circle that bleeds off the right edge. B: Edges are cleanly aligned, but the quote is smaller and a large dead gap separates the quote mark from the text. The logo is jammed directly under the attribution, so it reads as part of the text block and not as a brand sign-off. The bottle is small, off-centre and left in a floating circle with empty space to its right, and its 'SOLSTICE' label is tiny and hard to read.

A keeps a sensible left-to-right order: logo, headline, SAVE badge, body, CTA, product at the right edge. Flaws: the product is a tiny sliver jammed against the right edge and its label is unreadable; the badge floats in the gap between the headline and the body copy, away from the product; the body copy is small; the logo is tiny. B has a clearly broken order and brand treatment: the SAVE badge sits left of the headline and touches the edge. The logo is enlarged to a big circle in the middle that competes with the headline, and it sits between the product and the copy. The product is tiny and cramped beside the logo. The body copy is wrapped into a narrow column crammed against the CTA, and the headline wraps to an orphaned 'repeat'. B is more chaotic overall.

A has a strong headline and a big CTA, with the shoe at the top. Flaws: the subcopy is indented and misaligned with the headline, the LIMITED badge and CTA sit crowded and uneven, and the bottom 30% is dead space. B has a tiny headline, a small CTA and a tiny badge. The gaps are huge, the CTA and badge are scattered and unaligned, and the hierarchy is weak because the shoe dominates and the message is lost.

A: the dark header band stops short of the right edge (offset 10px left, gap on right), which looks like a bug. The headline is a dense, squeezed 6-line block, and the CTA sits high with a large dead gap above 'Ships late June', which is detached from its button. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow floats far above the headline. B: the header runs full-bleed and the headline wraps in 5 lines with good margins. 'Ships late June' stays tight under the CTA, and the legal text is tiny but contained. Flaws: the divider has been moved below the body copy, a large dead gap sits between headline and body, and the eyebrow-to-headline spacing is loose. The body and legal text are small. It is cleaner and more intentional than A.

The two are nearly identical: same orange field, white serif headline over a dark pill CTA, with no logo or imagery in either. A sits low. Its text block runs from about y=175 to 717, leaving a big empty band on top and only about 50px under the CTA, so it feels bottom-heavy and the CTA is crowded toward the edge. B's block is better centred, with about 135px above and 65px below, and its slightly larger gap before the CTA separates headline from action more clearly. Both have a tight 80px side margin on the headline, and the CTA label is small relative to the headline. B is marginally better balanced but still only acceptable.

A stacks eyebrow, big headline, body, CTA and bottle in a clear top-to-bottom order that suits a tall format. Text is large and the circle sits behind the bottle. Minor flaws: the body copy is tight to the CTA, and the bottle crowds the button and sits right of centre. B squeezes everything into the middle band and leaves the bottom third empty. Its text is small, the CTA is small, and the bottle floats unanchored beside the copy. The layout feels unbalanced and unfinished.

A: headline, body and CTA are tiny and the CTA and badge are barely noticeable. The CTA and LIMITED badge sit scattered far apart at the bottom. The body copy floats in a big dead zone with the shoe in the middle, so the hierarchy is weak. B: headline, CTA and body are large and legible, and the shoe is intact. But the body text is indented and misaligned with the headline and the LIMITED badge. The badge and CTA are cramped and uneven in height, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty, so the layout is top-heavy.

A keeps the original stack: wordmark, large bottle, a bold two-line headline, readable subcopy and a clearly sized CTA, with the circles kept as background accents. Flaws: the headline breaks as 'Garden-fresh / fizz' and leaves an orphaned word, the wordmark sits tight against the bottle cap and green circle, and there is dead space under the CTA. B shrinks everything. The bottle is small, the headline is much weaker, and the subcopy and CTA label are tiny and hard to read at this size. Large gaps separate the elements, so the content floats and the headline and CTA lose prominence. The green circle crowds the wordmark and the bottle, and the bottom third is loosely scattered.

A: the headline wraps to two lines and is huge, so it competes with the bag. The CTA is tiny and jammed right under 'fizz'. The headline runs almost to the right edge. The CITRINE logo sits on the green circle, and the logo and bag text are small and cramped. B: the single-line headline, bag, logo and CTA read left to right with a clear hierarchy and the CTA is a decent size. Flaws: the logo is small and floats far from the bag. The bag's label text is tiny. The circles are stacked at the left, leaving a dead area. The headline and CTA are crowded toward the right edge.

A: The headline wraps to two lines and leaves 'fizz' orphaned on its own line. The CTA sits only about 20px below it, with a large dead band under the CTA. The bag is a small, proportional copy of the original, and the circles are cropped awkwardly. B: The headline stays on one line with comfortable side margins, and the bag is larger and keeps its aspect ratio, so the product is the clear focal point. Flaws: the CTA is jammed about 15px under the headline and sits close to the bottom edge, the olive circle sits near the CTA's left edge, and the CTA label is small. Overall B reads more intentionally.

A keeps the original reading order: logo, eyebrow, headline, body. The headline is readable and the CTA is clear. Flaws: the body copy is jammed right under the headline. The CTA sits isolated on the right with a stray divider above it. The top-right is dead space, and the logo bar is cropped at the left edge. B has a better-sized CTA but is cramped and jumbled. The oversized headline runs close to the top edge and the body is jammed under it. The body text nearly touches the CTA. The eyebrow 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' is orphaned at the bottom-left, below the headline, and butts against the body text. The logo floats mid-left on a clipped white bar, and a stray rule sits under it. The hierarchy and grouping are broken.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark is stranded off-axis under the circle, and the heading, body, badges and CTA all sit on different left/right edges. The badges are jammed against each other and the right edge, and the CTA is right-aligned and offset from the copy. The result reads as scattered and ragged. B: it has a clear top-to-bottom flow of brand, headline, product, body, then a CTA row, and the product is large and centered. Flaws: the headline is indented and not aligned with the left margin or the centered brand, the CTA is a small button in a row with the badges so it is not dominant, and the CTA text is tiny. Dead space between the body and the buttons.

A keeps the circle-and-can illustration intact and the same design identity. The CTA is large and clear and the headline dominates. Flaws: GLACIER is centered oddly over the headline instead of aligned with it, the badges and CTA form a cramped right column with a big gap before it, the can is small, and the badge text is tiny. B separates the can from its circle: the circle is empty on the left and the can floats on the far right, which breaks the key imagery. B also puts the brand name below the headline, so the reading order is wrong, and the CTA is a small button no bigger than the badges. The body and badge text are tiny, and the text block is crammed against the bottom edge with a wide dead gap on the right.

A keeps headline, tagline and CTA as one centred stack with a big, clear full-width CTA. Flaws: the headline breaks into five lines with 'and a / little' choppy, it sits almost against the top edge, the CTA is slightly tight to the tagline, and there is dead space at the bottom. B splits the headline from its supporting copy: the tagline and CTA are pushed to the bottom edge with a big empty gap in between. The tagline is tiny, wraps to two lines and sits in an awkward row beside the CTA, which is small and close to the bottom edge. The hierarchy and grouping are broken.

A keeps the original's grouping (LIMITED badge beside the CTA, centred under the headline), with good headline size and a legible button. Flaws: the content is crammed toward the top with a large dead band below, and the badge is tiny and tilted. B's headline is huge and nearly touches the left and right edges, with almost no margin. The CTA text is small and the CTA and badge are split far apart, with the badge floating at the right, so the grouping is lost. The bottom row also feels disconnected from the headline.

A: the CTA is crammed into the top-left corner against the canvas edge and is tiny, and the LIMITED badge sits loosely under it. The CTA comes before the headline in reading order, and the headline floats mid-canvas with large dead areas above and below. B: the headline is large and dominant, and the badge and CTA sit below it in the original order. Flaws: the headline wraps awkwardly into five lines ("and a" / "little"), the headline's left margin is tight, the badge is loosely attached to the CTA, and there is dead space at the bottom.

A: everything is small and floats mid-canvas with huge dead bands above and below; the headline is tiny, the faint circle sits stray at the top-left, the badge and CTA are scattered far from the headline, and the bottle is cramped at the left edge. B: much larger headline, badge and CTA with better legibility and hierarchy, and the bottle is bigger. But all content is crammed into the top half with a large empty bottom, the bottle touches the top and left edges, the headline and bottle are jammed together, and the NEW badge and CTA are not aligned with the headline. B is still the less bad.

A scatters tiny fragments across a huge empty canvas: the headline is small and stranded top-left, the badge and CTA float disconnected on the right, and the tagline is orphaned bottom-right below the CTA. The reading order is jumbled and the phone is not tied to anything. B has a clear top-to-bottom flow of headline, tagline, badge and CTA, with large legible type, a strong CTA and correct fonts and colours. Its flaws: the phone and circle are cramped into the top-left corner and nearly touch the edge, the circle is clipped, the tagline is indented off the headline's left edge, the CTA is right-aligned while the text is left-aligned, and the badge crowds the CTA.

A stacks phone, large two-line headline, subline, then badge and CTA in a clear top-to-bottom order with strong hierarchy and a big CTA. Flaws: the phone is cropped at the top edge and its circle is clipped, the subline is indented off the headline's left edge, the badge and CTA are not aligned, and there is a dead band at the bottom. B scatters the elements: the headline is tiny and detached, the badge floats alone, the CTA is small, and the subline is tiny and far from the headline in the bottom-right corner. The right half is mostly empty, the hierarchy is weak and the grouping is lost.

A: reading order is broken — the attribution sits in the middle, detached from the quote, with the big logo wedged between the text and the product. The quote is squeezed into a narrow four-line column and the quote mark floats far above it, so the logo competes with the headline. B: keeps the original order of quote mark, quote, attribution, then product, with a sensible two-line quote and the same left-to-right flow. Flaws: the logo is tiny, clipped and has a cut-off 'E' in its wordmark. The quote mark is offset from the text edge, the left margins are inconsistent, the product circle crowds the right edge, and there is dead space below the attribution.

A: quote mark, headline and attribution form a clear left block with a good size step. The product circle sits at right, and the logo floats awkwardly in the middle. The bottle label is tiny and the quote mark is slightly crowded against the headline. B: attribution is jammed against the left canvas edge with almost no margin. It is also far from the quote, the quote mark floats detached, and the logo sits randomly in the middle. The large grey circle runs behind the text and the layout is ragged and unaligned.

A: the quote is tiny at this banner size. The bold attribution runs under it almost to the bottom edge, so the vertical spacing is cramped. The quote mark is crammed into the top-left corner, and the SOLSTICE logo is missing. B: it reads left to right in three clear columns (quote mark, quote, attribution, product), and the quote is larger and more legible. Flaws: the 3-line quote nearly touches the top and bottom edges. The attribution is as heavy as the quote, which weakens the hierarchy. The logo is dropped and the product bottle is small.

A keeps the original order (quote mark, quote, attribution, product, logo) with a small quote mark, a readable quote, and the lime attribution beneath it. Flaws: the attribution is very wide for the canvas and nearly touches the side margins, the logo is tiny and crammed against the circle, and the product label is illegible. B puts the attribution above the quote, which breaks the reading order. B's quote mark is oversized and competes with the headline, and the attribution is tiny and unreadable. B's logo sits awkwardly between the quote and the product, and the circle crops the product. B is the weaker resize.

A keeps the original's structure: quote mark, quote, attribution and logo stacked on the left, with the can in a circle on the right. Flaws: the circle is cropped by the right edge, the can is small inside it, and the quote text is only moderately sized. B is cramped. The logo sits on the attribution line and reads as part of it, with an awkward gap. The headline wraps to four ragged lines, the left column is jammed toward the bottom, and the quote mark is far from the text. The circle is better contained and the can is larger, but the grouping is worse and the margins are tight.

A keeps a clear left headline, steps in order 01-03 and a CTA, but the CTA is jammed at the bottom edge and the headline sits tight to the CTA. The fine print is tiny and runs right beside the button, and the bag is cropped by the circle and bottom. B has a good large headline, but the steps are scattered and out of sequence (01, 02 on top, 03 below), and the 01 and 03 text is tiny and hard to read. Its logo is shrunk to a speck on a clipped circle, the CTA floats far right, and the legal text is illegible.

A: headline is a clean, balanced 4-line block with good margins, but the tagline is a tiny 2-line fragment crammed beside the CTA at the bottom, leaving a large dead gap between headline and action and a weak grouping. B: the headline is huge and nearly touches the side edges ("botanicals" is almost edge to edge), the 'and a / little' breaks are awkward with a short ragged 5-line stack, the top margin is cramped, and a large empty strip sits at the bottom, so the composition is top-heavy. B does keep the tagline and CTA grouped and stacked in a clear order, with a big, prominent CTA. A reads as calmer and more designed, while B is closer to the original grouping but has crowding and poor margins. It is close; A is slightly safer on margins and wrapping.

A keeps the original order of headline, then LIMITED badge, then CTA, in one grouped stack. The headline is large and readable, and the CTA is a clear button. Flaws: the headline stacks up to five lines with a 'little' / 'sunshine.' ragged rag and nearly touches the top edge. The badge is left-aligned and off-axis from the centred CTA. The bottom ~25% is empty. B throws the headline into the lower-middle at small size. It puts the CTA and badge as tiny, cramped fragments jammed against the top-left edge, which makes the CTA buried and the hierarchy and reading order inverted. It also leaves large dead areas above and below the headline.

A: product in a full circle is large and balanced, quote text bigger and legible. Flaws: the logo is jammed next to the attribution on one line, so brand and credit read as one cluster. The quote block sits low and tight against the bottom, and the quote mark floats with a big gap above it. B: clean left-to-right flow, and the logo has its own spot bottom-left like the original. Flaws: the product circle is clipped at the right and bottom edges, the product is small, and the quote text is smaller. The quote mark is detached from the text, and the left block is top-heavy with dead space.

A: The headline is readable and centered, and the body copy and CTA are grouped in a right column. But the logo is stranded in a dark block at top-left, a stray orange divider floats at the far right, and the body copy is tiny. The CTA is small and the legal text is microscopic and crammed at the bottom. The hierarchy is passable but the layout is scattered. B: The headline is large and dominant. But the logo is a tiny dot in a dark panel, the orange divider is detached under it, and the CTA is a tiny pill buried at the bottom right. The body copy is a cramped narrow column and the legal text is illegible. The headline nearly touches the body column, the dark panel is mostly empty, and the CTA is the weakest element.

A keeps a clear order (logo, headline, body, tags, CTA) with a large CTA. Flaws: the circle crowds the GROVE logo, the body copy sits very close to the pills, the right-aligned pills and CTA are misaligned with the left-aligned text, and the bottom margin is tight. B shrinks the CTA to a tiny pill the same size as the tags, so it is buried among four equal chips. B also puts the CTA above the body copy, which breaks reading order, leaves a large dead gap, and sets the body text far from the headline. B's headline and image are good, but the hierarchy failure is worse.

A: the headline is huge, wraps to three lines and nearly fills the canvas height, so it dominates and crowds the tagline. The CTA is demoted to a tiny pill in a row with the badges, so the hierarchy is wrong. The phone is small and pushed into the corner, the tagline is cramped, and the bottom edge is tight. B: it keeps the original structure of phone on the left and a text stack on the right, with a clear headline and a prominent CTA. Flaws: the SOLSTICE label is centred while everything else is left-aligned, the tagline is indented a few pixels off the left edge, the CTA sits very close to the bottom edge, and the badges and CTA are tightly stacked.

A keeps the LIMITED badge and CTA together as in the original, with a big headline and a prominent CTA. Flaws: the headline is cramped to the top edge, there is a large empty band at the bottom, and the badge is tiny and tucked next to the CTA. B has a bigger headline with a small, weak CTA. Its LIMITED badge is detached and floats far from the button, so the grouping is lost, the row is unbalanced, and the CTA is buried under the oversized headline.

A: the elements are scattered across the canvas. Large dead gaps separate the headline, the subcopy and the pills. The CTA sits beside the subcopy, with the subcopy bottom-aligned to it, and the pill order is reversed from the original. The brand name floats on the circle, disconnected from the headline. The pills are tiny and there is no reading flow. B: the content forms one cohesive left-aligned stack: brand, a bigger headline, subcopy, then CTA, which is a clear hierarchy and reading order. Flaws: the headline overlaps the circle edge, which is acceptable. The CTA is oddly offset and jammed close to the subcopy. The pills are staggered at ragged, uneven widths and positions, with the orange pill off-axis. The pill order is reversed and the bottom third is empty. B is still the less bad of the two.

A: headline wraps cleanly in two lines, with a clear brand, headline, subline, CTA, pills order. Flaws: the CTA is jammed up against the subline and sits off-axis, the pills are staggered and ragged, the right-hand space is uneven, and the bottom-right circle is a tiny stray. B: the headline is large but 'Summer / flavours are here' leaves the brand line cramped against the top edge. The subline is squeezed into a narrow 3-line column beside the CTA. The pills are stacked in a confusing zigzag, with 'Honey Rosemary' placed before 'Blood Orange' (original order broken). The CTA and the pale circle overlap awkwardly, and the 'Cucumber Mint' pill sits on the circle. The layout feels crammed and arbitrary.

A: the flavour pills are shuffled (Honey Rosemary first, Blood Orange wrapped alone on a second row), and the pill order no longer matches the original. The CTA is oversized and competes with the headline, which is stacked over three lines. The circle bleeds behind the CTA and pills, and the legal text is tiny and cramped. B: it keeps the original left-to-right structure, with a one-line headline, the pills in the original order and a clear CTA. Flaws: the CTA is jammed right next to the subhead on the same baseline and looks crowded, the right circle is awkwardly cut and partly overlaps the CTA, the legal text is very small, and the lower area feels loose.

A keeps the headline large and the CTA/NEW badge legible, with the bottle in a circle at top. Flaws: the bottom 40% is empty, the ragged right-aligned buttons don't align with the left-aligned headline, NEW sits above the CTA in an odd order, and the circle crops against the top edge/overlaps the faint circle. B has a strong hero bottle, but the headline is tiny and weak at the top, and NEW and Try It are minuscule and far apart at the bottom, with the CTA buried and unaligned. The huge circle dominates and hierarchy is wrong.

A keeps the wide-banner structure but sits small in the vertical middle of a 768x198 canvas, leaving large dead bands above and below. The phone is tiny, the headline and subline are modest, and the badge and CTA are small and far from the copy. B scales everything up and fills the canvas, so the headline, phone and CTA have clear weight. B's flaws: the phone and its circle are jammed against the left edge and nearly clipped at the top and bottom. The badge sits low and almost touches the CTA. The bottom margin is tight and the left and right edges are uneven.

A keeps quote, attribution and can with clear hierarchy, but the attribution is jammed against the bottom edge, the block is cramped vertically and the logo is missing. B wraps the quote into three lines filling the full height with no margin, drops the attribution, leaves a dead gap in the middle with an illegible tiny logo, and the can is lost in a dark circle.

A keeps the original structure (phone left, text column right) with a clear headline and CTA. Flaws: the SOLSTICE wordmark is centered while the rest of the text is left-aligned, the tagline is indented off the left edge, the badges sit tight under the tagline, and the phone is cramped against the top and bottom edges. B has a hierarchy and grouping failure: the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill in the same row as the badges, so it is buried and no longer dominant. The headline wraps awkwardly to three lines, with 'back' orphaned, and fills the left half. The tagline is squeezed into a narrow three-line column, and the badge text is tiny and cramped. The layout is unbalanced and reads as a different design.

A: the body copy is jammed against the CTA, and the headline is tight against the SOLSTICE wordmark. The pills are cramped and arranged in a staggered 2-1 pattern, with Cucumber Mint pushed over the peach circle. The CTA sits too close to the copy, and the whole layout is crowded into the top-left and middle. B: the headline, subhead and wordmark have clean hierarchy and a shared left edge. The CTA and pills are three stacked rows with ragged, almost-aligned left edges, and the CTA is not clearly separated from the pills. The circle motif is reduced to a tiny peach blob in the corner, and the subhead is small. B is still more orderly and readable than A.

A: the CTA 'Find It Near You' is shrunk into a pill at the top-left, ahead of the headline, so the reading order is broken. The badge row wraps and misaligns, and the can is tiny. The big circle is cut off and sits behind the headline and tagline, which hurts legibility. The brand name 'GLACIER' falls below the headline, and there is a large dead area at the bottom. B: it keeps the circle-and-can hero, a brand-headline-copy-badges-CTA order, and a prominent CTA. Flaws: the text column has an awkward indent. The badges and CTA are offset and not aligned to the copy's left edge. 'GLACIER' floats alone at the top, detached from the headline. There is a big empty gap at the top right and bottom left, and the can sits slightly off-centre in its circle.

A: the phone is tiny and jammed against the left edge, with a large empty gap before the text. The SOLSTICE logo sits tight against the headline. The two badges and the CTA are almost the same size as each other, so the CTA is not distinct. The headline is small, and the CTA sits cramped near the bottom edge. B: the headline is large and clear, the phone is better proportioned, and the CTA is prominent. Flaws: the SOLSTICE logo is tiny and weak, and the tagline is crammed at the top, touching the canvas edge. The badges are scattered and out of the original order, with SUMMER ONLY below the CTA and BACK BY DEMAND off to the side. The right cluster is tight and the left side has big dead space.

A keeps the original stacked centred order, but the headline sits about 10px from the top edge and the CTA about 10px from the bottom, so it's cramped. The subline is tiny, and the stack doesn't use the banner's width, so it reads as a squashed copy. B uses a left-to-right banner structure with a large, dominant headline, which fits the format. However, the headline nearly touches the left edge and sits close to the subline and CTA on the right. The subline wraps into an awkward two-line fragment, and the CTA text is very small. The side column is crowded and the CTA is weak, though B is more intentional overall.

A: the layout is ragged and misaligned. SOLSTICE is indented relative to the headline, and the subhead is indented a third way. The CTA floats off-axis. The three pills are staggered at different left edges, with HONEY ROSEMARY orphaned on a second row. Headline text sits across the overlapping circles, and the content is jammed into a cramped block. B: there is a clean shared left margin, and the headline, subhead, CTA and pills are in a clear top-to-bottom order. The pills sit in one row, with a bottom margin that is a bit large. Flaws: the pill order is reversed from the original, the headline overlaps the big circle, the gap between headline and subhead is large, the pills are small, and the CTA is not aligned with the pill row.

A keeps the original order (eyebrow, headline, subline, CTA, product, footer) with a big headline and a large CTA. Flaws: 'WEEKEND ONLY' and the headline sit on the circle edge, the headline is jammed near the right edge, the gap between CTA and product is awkward, and the bottle is small. B moves 'WEEKEND ONLY' below the headline and merges it with the fine print, so the eyebrow loses its role and the reading order is jumbled. The headline is smaller and sits on the circle, the CTA is cut off from its copy at the bottom, and there are large dead areas at the top and between the groups.

A: the CTA button butts against the '20% off' headline and sits beside 'Every mixed case', and the legal line is jammed under both with no spacing. The eyebrow is left-offset, nothing shares an edge, and the shoe is tiny and clipped by the circle. B: the layout is clean and the text doesn't collide. But the CTA sits on the left, before the headline, which breaks reading order, and the legal line is microscopic. The shoe is squashed and the left and right sides are unbalanced, with a large dead gap in the middle.

A: the shoe is stuck at the bottom-left of the circle and not aligned with it. The 'Weekend Only' label floats alone far from the headline, and the legal text is microscopic and unreadable. A dark artifact sits beside the button, and the layout is scattered with big dead areas. B: the text stack is more coherent, with the headline large and the legal text readable. But the stack is ragged, because 'Weekend Only', the headline, the subline and the button start at different x positions. The legal line is jammed against the button's edge and sits baseline-low. The circle is cropped at the top edge and the shoe is lopsided, with the CTA at the lower left, so it is flawed but more usable.

A keeps a strong large '20% off' headline and the circle-behind-bottle motif, but the eyebrow sits inline with the headline, the copy is jammed against the CTA, and the bottle crowds the top and bottom edges. B shrinks the headline, floats it low and misaligned with the eyebrow, leaves the body copy detached, and puts the bottle in the middle with the CTA stranded at the right. The circle is cropped into an unrelated corner blob, so hierarchy and grouping are weak and the design looks scattered.

A: product circle is cropped off the top-left corner and the bottle is tiny, so the product is nearly lost. The NEW badge and CTA are oversized and compete with the headline. The subhead is indented and misaligned with the headline, and the lower right is a stack of mismatched pills with a big empty gap. B: the product is large, whole and centred, the headline is clear on the left margin, and the bottom row is tidy. But the headline is small for a portrait canvas, the subhead is tiny, and the CTA and badge are small and spread across a single cramped row. The oversized circle dominates and the hierarchy is weak. It is cleaner and more intentional than A, though still not shippable.

A: the headline is tiny and floats at the top while a huge bottle circle dominates the canvas, so the hierarchy is inverted. The circle is oversized, a stray faded circle sits in the top-left corner, and NEW and Try It are small and scattered at the bottom with no grouping. The big empty areas are unbalanced. B: the headline is large and readable, and the bottle sits in its circle top-left. The CTA and NEW badge are clear, right-aligned and grouped. Flaws: the faded decorative circle overlaps the product circle awkwardly, the bottle is small, the NEW badge is as prominent as the CTA, and there is a dead area bottom-left.

A keeps the headline large and prominent with a clear CTA, but the product bottle is clipped and its label cut off. The cream circle is a stray fragment at the bottom-left. 'Out now.' sits low, detached from the headline with a big gap, and the dark text on orange is only moderate contrast. B shrinks the headline to a small size, leaving large dead space. The CTA is tiny and far from the copy, and the bottle is cropped by the cream circle with a messy overlap. Both lose the original's tidy left-to-right banner, but B has weak hierarchy and looks sparse and unintentional.

A: the "missing asset" placeholder box is large and sits at the bottom-right, colliding with the tagline and adding clutter. The pills are stacked at different widths and ragged-aligned, and the RSVP button sits alone with its tagline crammed beneath. The headline and date are fine, but the badges read as three competing buttons. B: the layout is tidier. Headline, date and details are left-aligned, and the badges and RSVP are grouped in two rows. Flaws: the placeholder is a small red box overlapping the bottom of the tagline, and the logo is tiny. "FREE ENTRY" next to the CTA competes with it. There is a large dead gap above the product and the product is small. Overall B is cleaner and less cluttered than A, though both are still flawed.

A keeps a clear left-to-right flow: headline on the left, then date/pills, phone and CTA. Flaws: the headline touches the edge of the circle and the date block, the fine print is tiny, the broken partner-logo placeholder is tucked at the right edge, and the right column is cramped. B has a huge missing-asset placeholder box that dominates the right third and is visibly broken. Its headline is forced into a stacked 'Sunset / Sessions' that overflows the circle, 'Reserve a spot' is orphaned from the RSVP button, and the pills are scattered in a jumbled 2x2. The CTA is also small and the reading order is confused.

A: the headline wraps to two lines and nearly fills the circle, while the italic tagline is squeezed into a 4-line narrow column. The RSVP pill is tiny and the legal text is microscopic. A huge grey placeholder box dominates the right side, and the phone is wedged in. The reading order is jumbled and the layout is cramped and scattered. B: it keeps a clear left-to-right flow from logo and headline to the date, pills, a large RSVP button and the phone. The tagline sits on one line below the headline. Flaws: the headline is close to the circle edge and the left margin, the placeholder image is small and crammed against the phone at the right edge, the legal text is tiny, and the middle column is a bit tight. It is still much cleaner than A.

A has broken reading order: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits below the headline, the CTA line 'Reserve a spot...' is jammed between the tagline and the time with no button, and the date/time/tagline are cramped with inconsistent alignment. The RSVP is demoted to a tiny pill in a cluster at the bottom, and there is a large dead zone around the phone. B keeps the original order (presents, headline, tagline, date, time, badges, phone, big RSVP button, URL), with a clear hierarchy and a strong CTA. Its flaws: the broken-image placeholder is crowded next to the URL, the phone is small and sits awkwardly near the badges, and the sub-copy is small.

A: the legal line butts right against the Shop Sale button with no gap, and the headline, subline and eyebrow are misaligned (eyebrow indented, body offset). The shoe is pushed to the bottom right and clipped by the circle edge, with a big empty gap in the middle. Hierarchy is still readable. B: the legal text is microscopic and illegible, and it sits jammed next to the button. The eyebrow is detached from the headline at far left, and the shoe sits awkwardly at the bottom of the circle, with the circle's left edge cut off. The button also has an odd left edge artifact. The structure is split and unbalanced, which makes B worse.

A: the headline is small and sits low, misaligned with the eyebrow at the top and with the body copy beside it. The body copy is tiny and floats in the middle, and the CTA is detached from its copy. The circle is cropped to a stray blob in the corner and no longer sits behind the bottle. Overall it looks scattered with no common baseline. B: the large headline and CTA are clear, the bottle sits on its circle as in the original, and the text is readable. Flaws: the eyebrow is jammed against the headline on one line, the headline is not aligned with the left edge, the CTA sits awkwardly beside the body copy, and the bottle is cramped against the top and right edges.

A: headline is tiny and stranded at top-left, while the huge circle and bottle dominate and the bottle fills with dead orange, so the product outweighs the message. The bottom row is cramped, with the NEW pill, CTA and 8px-scale tagline strung out and misaligned, so the hierarchy is wrong. B: the headline is large and clear and the CTA is prominent, but the logo circle is clipped at the top-left corner and the bottle is tiny. The tagline is indented and doesn't share the headline's left edge, and the NEW and Try It buttons are staggered and right-aligned, so alignment is ragged. Still, it reads in order and its hierarchy is stronger than A's.

A keeps a clear left-to-right flow: the headline is dominant, the date, time, tags and RSVP button are grouped in the middle, and the phone sits on the right. Flaws: the partner-logo placeholder overlaps the phone edge, the legal text is tiny, the headline crowds the left edge and circle, and the right edge is tight. B has a huge grey placeholder box dominating the right side, with illegible legal text above it. B also stacks 'Live music and rooftop pours' in a narrow four-line column, and the 'RSVP Free' CTA is shrunk into a tag pill with the tags and loses its prominence. The headline is also cramped against the circle.
